title: Legal Forwarding Agreements General Terms — Suspension of Forwarding and Termination
content:
## Clause on suspension

**(a) Grounds.** Forwarding under an agreement of the Legal Forwarding Agreements is suspended when the cost deposit has stayed below the programme's minimum deposit balance for more than the programme's shortfall period in calendar days, or when the linked Contingency Placement Agreement leaves both active and placement hold.

**(b) Resumption.** Forwarding resumes when the cause is cleared.

**(c) Effect.** Suspension stops new matters only; open matters continue.

A suspension is recorded with its date and its reason — a deposit shortfall, or the contingency agreement no longer being open. While suspended, the agreement shows the status suspended; on resumption it shows active again.

### Reading the shortfall ground

"More than" the shortfall period is strictly longer than it. On an abstract count with a shortfall period of N calendar days: a deposit that has stayed below the minimum for exactly N days has not stayed below it for more than N days, so this ground is not yet met; once it has stayed below for N days and one more day, the ground is met.

### Reading the contingency ground

| Status of the linked Contingency Placement Agreement | Ground for suspension under (a)? |
|---|---|
| Active | No |
| Placement hold | No |
| Any status other than active or placement hold | Yes |

## Clause on termination

**(d) Notice and minimum term.** The client terminates on the programme's notice period in calendar days, never effective before the programme's minimum agreement term in months after signing.

**(e) When termination takes effect.** A termination takes effect only when the handling date is later than the notice period counted from the date the client's notice was received. The notice period is the programme's notice period in calendar days, the day after the notice date being day one.

**(f) Matters in suit.** Matters already in suit continue for the programme's tail period in calendar days after termination, after which open matters are closed as recalled without the recall fee.

A termination is recorded with the date the client's notice was received and the date the termination takes effect; it applies whether the agreement is active or suspended at the time, and the agreement's status becomes terminated.

### Notice period on hypothetical dates

The anchor is the notice-received date shown in Ridgeline's records. Day one is the day after it; the termination takes effect only on a handling date later than the last day of the period — the last day itself is too early.

| Notice received | Notice period | Last day of the period | Handling date on the last day | Handling date the day after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 June | 30 days | 1 July (2 June is day 1) | not yet effective | may take effect (2 July) |
| 1 June | 90 days | 30 August (30 June is day 29, 31 July day 60) | not yet effective | may take effect (31 August) |

Clause (d) applies alongside: whatever the notice date, the termination is never effective before the minimum agreement term, counted in months from signing, has run.

### After termination

| Matter position at termination | What happens |
|---|---|
| Already in suit | continues for the programme's tail period in calendar days |
| Still open when the tail period ends | closed as recalled, without the recall fee |

## Points of judgement

- *Does a suspension close the client's open matters?* No. Suspension stops new matters only; open matters continue.
- *Is a termination effective on the last day of the notice period?* No. It takes effect only when the handling date is later than the notice period.
